state_reported: open state (Biswas et al. 2025: 'Our native, untruncated structures of hNav1.5 are captured in the open state')
active_sites_note: Nav1.5 is a channel, not an enzyme: UniProt Q14524 lists no active site.

sites.name: IFM motif
sites.definition: Biswas et al. 2025: 'the Isoleucine-Phenylalanine-Methionine (IFM) motif in the linker between D III and D IV ... crucial for fast inactivation'; located here by sequence search of UniProt Q14524 between S6 of repeat III (ends 1470) and S1 of repeat IV (starts 1529)
sites.source: Biswas R, López-Serrano AL, Purohit A, et al. Structural basis of human Nav1.5 gating mechanisms. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 2025;122(20):e2416181122. doi:10.1073/pnas.2416181122, PubMed 40366698, PMC12107192

membrane_normal_note: calculated: mean unit vector along the 24 UniProt transmembrane segments, each oriented from its cytoplasmic end to its extracellular end using the UniProt topological domain before it; 24 segments used. Points to the extracellular side.
tm_span_note: calculated: extent of the C-alpha atoms of UniProt-annotated transmembrane residues along the normal. This is the span of those residues, not a measured membrane thickness.
note: C-alpha positions in angstrom as deposited (model I of Biswas et al. 2025). Secondary structure from the file's HELIX and SHEET records. Repeats, membrane segments and topology from UniProt by residue number (numbering checked against the UniProt canonical sequence). Unmodelled regions are gaps.
